newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool prices drop six percent in week.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool prices drop six percent in week.

text.p: Australian wool prices dropped an unexpected six percent this week at sales in Sydney and Melbourne, the Australian Council of Wool Exporters said.
The council said the volatility which can affect auction prices was seen at its worst, with the six percent drop in prices on average following last week's jump of four percent.
"Such volatility harms everyone involved: growers, buyers and processors," the council said.
The eastern market indicator dropped 47 cents to end at 706 cents a kg clean, after touching a two-year high of 755 cents last week. There were no sales in Fremantle.
A total of 70,617 bales were offered with a pass in rate of 12.6 percent.
Wesfarmers Dalgety Ltd said the wool market's confidence and strength of the last five weeks was arrested as prices sharply corrected.

Wesfarmers said this was in response to the upward revised quantities on offer next week - 47 percent greater than originally rostered - which is a consequence of previous withheld grower stocks attracted to auction by the upturn in prices.
Wool International said that in the futures market, a total of 397 lots were traded in the 21 micron contract in the week ended June 26 and open interest increased by 80 contracts to close at 1,317.
The August contract closed 71 cents down at 855 cents a kg clean.
Wool International said its stockpile totalled 1,570,574 bales at June 26 after sales of 3,286 bales in the week.
Sales continue next week in Sydney, Melbourne and Fremantle with 136,490 bales rostered, up from an original quantity of about 80,000.
